quiz.title: Integration Exercise 7.4 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the standard special-form integrals from Exercise 7.4 — the arctan, arcsin and log formulas, plus completing the square. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths, Integrals of some particular functions (Ex 7.4)

questions.explanation: Here a² = 9, so a = 3. Using ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) + C gives (1/3) tan⁻¹(x/3) + C.
With a = 5, ∫ dx/√(a² − x²) = sin⁻¹(x/a) + C. There is no 1/a factor for this form, so the answer is sin⁻¹(x/5) + C.
The standard result is ∫ dx/(x² − a²) = (1/2a) log|(x − a)/(x + a)| + C, obtained by partial fractions.
∫ dx/(a² − x²) = (1/2a) log|(a + x)/(a − x)| + C. Note the numerator has (a + x); this differs from the x² − a² form.
With a = 4, ∫ dx/√(x² + a²) = log|x + √(x² + a²)| + C, so the answer is log|x + √(x² + 16)| + C.

questions.q: To evaluate ∫ dx/(x² + 6x + 13), the first step is to write the denominator as:
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x² + 6x + 13 = (x + 3)² + (13 − 9) = (x + 3)² + 4. Then use the arctan form with a = 2.
With a = 3, ∫ dx/√(x² − a²) = log|x + √(x² − a²)| + C, giving log|x + √(x² − 9)| + C.
Take 4 out: 9 − 4x² = 4(9/4 − x²), so the integral is (1/2) ∫ dx/√((3/2)² − x²) = (1/2) sin⁻¹(x/(3/2)) + C = (1/2) sin⁻¹(2x/3) + C.

faq.q: What does Exercise 7.4 of NCERT Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It covers integrals of some particular functions — the standard forms that produce inverse tangent, inverse sine and logarithm results, such as ∫ dx/(x² + a²), ∫ dx/√(a² − x²) and ∫ dx/(x² − a²), often after completing the square.

faq.q: How many standard formulas should I memorise for this exercise?
faq.a: There are six core formulas: the three log/partial-fraction forms for x² − a², a² − x² and the two square-root forms √(x² ± a²), plus the arctan and arcsin forms. Once you know these six, every question in Ex 7.4 reduces to matching a given integral to one of them.

faq.q: When do I need to complete the square?
faq.a: Whenever the denominator is a quadratic like x² + bx + c that is not already in x² ± a² form. Rewrite it as (x + b/2)² + k, substitute t = x + b/2, and the integral becomes one of the standard forms.

faq.q: What is the difference between the arctan and arcsin forms?
faq.a: The arctan form ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) has a plus sign and a full quadratic in the denominator. The arcsin form ∫ dx/√(a² − x²) = sin⁻¹(x/a) has a square root and a² minus x². Reading the sign and the square root correctly tells you which formula applies.
